checks.name: Rejected-operation failure atomicity and side-effect freedom
checks.method: read `ObservationHub::authenticate` (cpp 298-315), `poll` (cpp 519-534), `snapshot` (cpp 536-553), and `detach` (cpp 568-591); read `SyntheticObservationSink::connect`/`pull` (cpp 597-622); read `test_synthetic_sink_disconnect_isolation` (unit_tests.cpp 1215-1255) and `test_synthetic_sink_failure_isolation` (unit_tests.cpp 1258-1301); ran the unit executable
checks.result: pass: `poll` acquires the hub mutex, calls `authenticate` first, and returns `invalid_tap_handle` with no mutation when authentication fails (foreign/stale/closed handle); on `no_record` it returns before touching any record; on `accepted` it copies the record and advances `head`/`size` under the same lock. `connect()` only reads through const `snapshot` and mutates the sink's own `connected_` flag. The disconnect-isolation case proves a disconnected pull leaves the observed tap's `queued`/`accepted`/`dropped` unchanged and the retained sequence-1 record still pullable by the other sink and after reconnect; the failure-isolation case proves the foreign hub's slot keeps `accepted == 0`/`queued == 0`, the recreated slot keeps its own zero counters, and the stale `connect()` leaves the sink disabled. All rejects are side-effect free and atomic before mutation.

checks.name: Visible consumer counter semantics and accounting identity
checks.method: read `SyntheticSinkCounters` (hpp 767-777) and `counters()` (hpp 837); read `SyntheticObservationSink::pull` (cpp 606-622); confirmed `ObservationStatus::succeeded()` is `outcome == accepted` (hpp 194) and that `poll` can only return `accepted`/`no_record`/`invalid_tap_handle`; read `test_synthetic_sink_visible_counters` (unit_tests.cpp 1151-1212); ran `strings` on the built `xverse_xcom_observation_unit_tests`
checks.result: pass: `pull` increments exactly one counter on the actual outcome -- disconnected short-circuit -> `disconnected`, `accepted` -> `pulled`, `no_record` -> `empty`, and the final branch -> `failed` (reachable only for `invalid_tap_handle` because `poll` has no other failing return). `connect()`/`disconnect()` change no counter. `counters()` is `noexcept` and returns a value copy (no hub view). The case drives two record pulls, one empty pull, one disconnected pull, and one stale-handle pull and asserts the identity `pulled + empty + disconnected + failed == 5 == attempts` plus `connected()` after each transition. The new assertion strings are present in the built binary, so the case executes rather than being dead code.

checks.result: pass: `disconnect()` mutates only `connected_` and never calls the hub; a disconnected `pull` returns `sink_disconnected` without calling `poll`. checks.name: Failure isolation for stale/foreign/closed exact handles
checks.method: read `test_synthetic_sink_failure_isolation`; ran the unit executable; re-read `authenticate` and `ObservationHub::make_handle`/constructor (cpp 290-295, 79) to confirm per-hub instance ids are unique
checks.result: pass: `hub_instance_id_` is a monotonically increasing atomic, so a foreign hub's handle never authenticates. A sink constructed over a foreign hub's handle reports `invalid_tap_handle` with `failed == 1` and no record; the foreign hub keeps `accepted == 0`/`queued == 0` and the foreign handle authenticates at neither hub. After `detach` of the observed tap, a pull reports `invalid_tap_handle` with `failed == 1`; the recreated slot keeps its own zero counters; `connect()` on the stale handle is refused (`invalid_tap_handle`) and leaves the sink disabled. No tap, generation, counter, or record is mutated.
